messages:
mara: Heads up — CI on main is red for the `api-image` job. Build completes but docker push fails at manifest finalize with 401. Logs attached: https://ci.redwood.internal/2359/job/422/log

devon: ugh. can you paste the exact error snippet? 401 on finalize usually means registry token issue or expired creds.

mara: Sure — from the job:
```
Error: denied: authentication required
level=error msg=manifest put https://registry.redwood.internal/v2/redwood/api/manifests/latest: unauthorized: authentication required
```

devon: thanks. ops-bot, any recent credential rotations?

ops-bot: notice: registry credentials rotated for ci-service-account at 2359988000. Tokens should have propagated by 2359990000.

liam: hmm, CI shows a retry loop then 401. Could be the image was built with layer squashing enabled in the new Dockerfile change — that sometimes invalidates existing upload session assumptions in our upload proxy.

sophie: @liam which Dockerfile change? I only touched a tiny chown reorder in #4219.

liam: there was also an experimental squash layer step merged in #4226 by @ken — it rewrites layers and changed content-length patterns. If the registry proxy caches chunk offsets it can cause EOF/401 on finalize.

mara: CI commit points to both PRs landing ~2h ago. Should we rerun without cache first?

devon: do a quick triage: 1) rerun pipeline with --no-cache (no layer cache) 2) if still 401, try pushing to staging registry to separate auth vs payload issues 3) bisect by reverting the squash commit locally and re-run.

mara: starting rerun with no-cache: `ci run pipeline -p api-image --build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=0 --no-cache`

ci-bot: retriggered pipeline 2359991125 by mara — queued on runner-r3

mara: rerun failed with same 401 during manifest put, but layers uploaded fine.

devon: that makes auth more likely. ops-bot can you confirm CI service account token in vault matches registry's accepted token?

ops-bot: checking... Vault secret for ci/registry-token last updated at 2359990900. Registry reports accepted tokens list updated at 2359989000. There is a mismatch; rotate job didn't pick up new token.

sophie: so the rotate job partially applied. Is there a manual hotfix?

ops-bot: manual fix: re-sync vault -> ci runners. Pushing new token now. ETA ~2m.

liam: while that's happening, can we try pushing to private staging registry to confirm? I can update CI to point to staging for a quick run.

mara: please do. switching target to registry-staging.redwood.internal in the pipeline and re-run.

ci-bot: retriggered pipeline 2359991189 by liam -> runner-r5

mara: staging push succeeded and manifest finalized. So payload/format is fine. This is definitely auth.

devon: OK — once ops-bot confirms token sync we should be green. Also open a follow-up to add a healthcheck after rotation that attempts a manifest put to catch this earlier.

ops-bot: token sync complete at 2359991240. CI runners reloaded credentials.

ci-bot: retriggered pipeline 2359991243 by mara -> runner-r2

mara: final run — push to prod registry now succeeded. Marking main green.

mara: action items: 1) ops: add post-rotation manifest probe (ops ticket OPS-987) 2) infra: revert experimental squash step from #4226 and move to feature branch until we handle proxy quirks (#4226-revert) 3) dev: add ci test pushing to staging registry during PRs so we catch auth vs payload earlier.

sophie: noted — I'll open the revert PR for #4226 and link OPs ticket.

devon: thanks all :thumbsup:

mara: closing the loop — main is green and I'm blasting a short postmortem in #postmortems later.
